absent: Numeric values of page shift, vdso data page count, vectors base address, and virtual memory flag bits.
Implementations of variable area install, special mapping install, unmapped area selection, and frame conversions.
Layouts of address space context, virtual area, special mapping, and loader structures beyond referenced fields.
Conditions controlling branch protection, SIMD capability, address authentication, and compat configuration.
Linker symbol addresses, segment alignments, cache sizes, and generated constants not shown in fragments.
Semantics of common time and random helpers, signal trampoline usage, and crash metadata consumers.

findings.text: A per-ABI descriptor holds a display name, start and end markers delimiting the resident code image, a page count derived at init, and a pointer to a special mapping descriptor used at install time.

A table fixed after init is indexed by an ABI selector with distinct native and compat members; the native slot is named for the standard vdso and the compat slot when enabled is named for the 32-bit vdso, each bounded by its own start and end markers.

Init validates that the image begins with ELF identification and fails otherwise, derives page count from image extent scaled by page size, allocates a page pointer list, populates it from consecutive frames beginning at the image start, and attaches the list to the ABI mapping descriptor.

Setup computes text length from stored page count and adds data pages to get total length, reserves an unmapped range, installs a variable area at its base, advances past data pages, records the resulting base as the process vdso pointer, then installs the code mapping readable and executable with branch protection when supported; any failure clears the vdso pointer and propagates the error.
When the vdso area moves, the current process context vdso address is updated to the new area start and success is reported; a parallel handler updates the compat sigpage address on move of its area.

Compat support defines three ordered slots for vectors, sigpage and vdso; vectors and sigpage each reference a single resident page with ABI visible names, sigpage and vdso each provide a move handler that keeps process context in sync.

The vectors page is a zeroed page with helper code copied to its tail when helpers are enabled, otherwise allocation is skipped; the sigpage is a fresh page first filled with a poison pattern and then overwritten at its start with sigreturn code.

Boot allocation proceeds from compat vdso image init to sigpage creation to vectors page creation, stopping on first error; per-process setup installs helpers at a fixed vectors base, optionally installs the compat vdso, then allocates and installs a sigpage and records its address.

Both the native and compat additional-pages entry points acquire the target address space write lock in killable mode before installing mappings and release it afterwards; if acquisition is interrupted they return without installing anything.
The native hook operates on the current process address space and delegates to shared additional-pages logic for the native ABI, returning its status to the program load path.
Native execution provides an additional-pages installer that the program loader calls to map variable and code areas for the new address space.
Compat execution provides an additional-pages installer that the program loader calls to map vectors, compat vdso and sigpage for a 32-bit address space.
User visible special mapping names are [vectors] for kuser helpers, [sigpage] for the sigreturn page, and [vdso] for both native and compat vdso images.
The compat sigpage poison word has value 0xe7fddef1 and is stored little endian to fill the page before sigreturn code is copied.

At boot the native mapping descriptor is linked to the native table slot before running shared image init, and the compat descriptor is linked to the compat slot when compat vdso is enabled before running the same init.
The vdso provides a sigreturn trampoline that requests realtime signal return service via supervisor call and must remain byte stable.

The no-stack block routine loads a fixed expansion constant plus key and counter nonce into vector state, iterates twenty rounds of add xor rotate with lane shuffles for each 64 byte block, adds the initial state to produce output, advances output and decrements the block count until done, writes back the updated counter, and clears vector registers holding sensitive material.
The native vdso exports clock gettime, gettimeofday and clock getres routines that forward directly to the corresponding common vdso helpers.
The 32-bit vdso exports clock gettime and getres in both 32-bit and 64-bit time forms plus gettimeofday, each forwarding to the matching common helper, and defines a 64-bit build marker.
Three ARM unwinding personality routines are present as no-operation placeholders that return immediately.

The vdso random routine uses an accelerated common helper when floating point and SIMD support is likely present, otherwise falls back to the system call; a probe with inverted length and empty buffer and flags reports unimplemented.

Crash dump metadata records address space width, module and vmalloc and vmemmap bounds, image offset, physical offset, current T1 size field extracted from system register, kernel slide, and pointer authentication mask which is zero when address authentication is unsupported.

The kernel link places entry at _text equal to the configured image virtual address, aliases jiffies to the 64-bit counter, discards interpreter dynamic symbol hash and ARM attribute sections, and sets PE file alignment to 512 bytes.

Text output groups interrupt softirq entry generic scheduler lock probe hypervisor and static call code, followed by read-only data, hypervisor data, GOT with a size check, non-executed trampoline hibernate kexec and idmap code, reserved page directories, init text data and percpu regions, relocations, writable data with hypervisor and MMU-off sections, padding, zero-init with page table area and early stack, then debug and module metadata.

Link time checks fail the build if hypervisor idmap text exceeds a page, idmap text crosses its 4K window, hibernate exit exceeds 4K or does not start at its suspend exit symbol, trampoline exceeds three pages, host and hypervisor BSS diverge, HEAD misaligns, page directory offsets mismatch, or kexec relocation exceeds its control page or mis-starts.

Vectors mapping omits future write permission to keep the page shared, while sigpage mapping retains future write permission to permit debugger breakpoints; vdso code is installed readable and executable and sealed as a system mapping, with branch protection enabled when the kernel supports it.
Total vdso reservation always covers code pages plus a fixed count of data pages, with variable area installed first and code following after the data reservation.

Image validation failure, page list allocation failure, unmapped area failure, and mapping install failure each abort setup with an error code and leave no vdso pointer installed; allocation helpers propagate out-of-memory without partial state.
Setup enforces at build time that the count of vdso data pages matches the generated page count constant.
